'Interactive Judge Tool'


This tool provides a visual representation of key MMA judging concepts. It illustrates the hierarchy of judging criteria, how those criteria apply to various fighting techniques, and how they influence scoring decisions. The values are relative, not absolute, and are intended to help judges understand how techniques contribute to scoring decisions.

It illustrates how Dominance is inversely proportionate to Duration. As the Dominance level goes up, the Duration requirement goes down



Suggestions for improvement are always welcome!

-----------------------------------------------------------


It's very challenging to teach MMA judging because there are so many scenarios, combinations of elements, and levels of effectiveness to measure
Scoring rounds are relative, subjective and at each judges discretion

Thinking about dominance - How, when and why to apply it while you are scoring a round

When I'm scoring a round, I'm assessing and evaluating effective strikes and effective grappling - It’s the top priority criteria for a reason
I don't have time to process the definition of domination, as they apply to striking and grappling, and apply it to the action I’m assessing,

I am assessing, evaluating and comparing the action in a small window, real-time, so I can track my score 100 percent of the time, without distraction


There will be challenging rounds that are difficult to determine if either fighter has an advantage
these are the times you





but the goal is to know my score at any given time throughout the round, without the need to process complex guidelines




I’m focussed on the real-time action


Dominance: When would you actually think about it and use it while scoring a round?



You don’t want to be processing definitions and guidelines while you’re scoring a round
You need to know them at a level, where you can apply them immediately in real-time, while scoring the round
These tools will help you absorb, analyze and retain the criteria and guidelines, so you can achieve this level


I think about duration when there isn't any damage. Has a fighter controlled, dominated,

When do I think about domination, aggressiveness or cage control ?




Interactive Judging Tool
When it comes to dominance without damage, I measure its effectiveness by first, determining the level of domination,
then factoring in the duration to justify a 10-8 score

I do not consider duration when evaluating damage, because it's effectiveness can happen in a split-second
Domination without damage however, is an element that can be measured by first, determining the level of domination, then factoring in the duration
If both domination and duration meet the judges requirements, it can justify a 10-8 score



You can vaguely, in a relaxed way, watch a round and determine which fighter score scored a 10-9 without the need to be so detailed…
BUT if you do practice watching intently with 100% laser focus, you’ll be more likely to have the skills to differentiate which fighter won the round,
when it's a razor, thin, close round or determining between a round goes from 10-9 to 10-8


Regarding the dominant/duration chart, the examples are illustrating the concept of the variable levels of dominance

Judge’s may have their own set of criteria that they use in those three levels, they should all be close from one judge to another, but there will be some overlap
